changes.before: 书里的人管他叫"鳗鱼"，那是小时候留下的一个绰号；而他的真名——如果他有过一个真名的话——书里从头到尾没有出现。

changes.before: 他是一个弃儿，是被人从孤儿院领出来的。领他的是一户住在卡米内拉的穷人家，那里有一栋破房子，一小块坡地，几只羊；领他的人后来被他叫作"教父"，那家还有两个女孩，他管她们叫姐姐。
changes.after: 他是一个弃儿。亚历山德里亚的医院把他交给一户住在卡米内拉的穷人家。那里有一栋两间屋带一间牲口棚的小房子，有一只山羊，还有一片长着榛树的坡地。领他的是维尔吉利娅和他后来叫作“教父”的那个人；家里还有两个女孩，他把她们当姐姐。
changes.zh_hant: 他是一個棄兒。亞歷山德里亞的醫院把他交給一戶住在卡米內拉的窮人家。那裡有一棟兩間屋帶一間牲口棚的小房子，有一隻山羊，還有一片長著榛樹的坡地。領他的是維爾吉利婭和他後來叫作“教父”的那個人；家裡還有兩個女孩，他把她們當姐姐。

changes.before: 而这家人领他，是因为每个月有一笔钱。那个年代的孤儿院有这么一项安排：把弃儿交给愿意抚养的农户，每月付一笔补贴；对一户穷得只有几只羊的人家来说，那笔钱不算多，而是一笔实实在在的进项。书里写得毫不避讳——这一家人拿了那笔钱，把他养到能干活；而等他长到能干活的年纪，那笔钱也就停了，因为那时候他不再是一笔收入，他成了一个劳力。后来这家人过不下去，把地卖了，搬走了，而他被留下，去别处做长工。
changes.after: 而这家人领他，是因为每个月有一笔钱。按他的回忆，亚历山德里亚的医院付这笔钱，家里去市镇公所领五里拉。对一户穷得只有一只羊的人家来说，钱不算多，却是一笔实实在在的进项。书里写得毫不避讳：这一家人拿了那笔钱，也指望等他大些，全家能一起干活。等他长大一点，补贴已经停了。后来“教父”带着两个女孩搬去了科萨诺，他留在这一带，去了别处做长工。

changes.before: 而每一步都是正当的。孤儿院在处理一个它养不起的孩子，那笔补贴让这个孩子有饭吃、有地方住，这比留在院里强；那户人家也没有虐待他——书里写他们对他不算坏，他跟那两个女孩一起长大，一起干活，一起挨饿。而在这一整套安排里，从来没有出现过一个问题：这个孩子是谁。他没有出生记录，没有父母的名字，没有姓；书里写他后来查过，查不出来，他只知道自己是从亚历山德里亚那边的医院来的，别的一概不知道。
changes.after: 而每一步都说得过去。医院给孩子找了地方，补贴也让他有饭吃、有地方住。书里写这家人对他不算坏，他跟两个女孩一起长大，一起干活，一起挨饿。而在这一整套安排里，始终没有弄清一个问题：这个孩子是谁。他不知道自己生在哪里，也不知道父母是谁。他去过亚历山德里亚的医院，镇公所的人还说公所里也许还存着他的材料。但有一份材料，与知道自己从哪里来，是两件事。
changes.zh_hant: 而每一步都說得過去。醫院給孩子找了地方，補貼也讓他有飯吃、有地方住。書裡寫這家人對他不算壞，他跟兩個女孩一起長大，一起幹活，一起挨餓。而在這一整套安排裡，始終沒有弄清一個問題：這個孩子是誰。他不知道自己生在哪裡，也不知道父母是誰。他去過亞歷山德里亞的醫院，鎮公所的人還說公所裡也許還存著他的材料。但有一份材料，與知道自己從哪裡來，是兩件事。

changes.before: 它不是一个名字，是一个说法；它的来历书里没有细讲，而任何一个绰号的功能都是一样的——它是别人给你的一个把手，方便他们叫你。一个有名字的人，那个名字是一份东西：它跟一个家族连着，跟一个出生的日子连着，跟一份记录连着，哪怕那个人死了，那个名字还在某个本子上。而一个绰号什么也不连，它只在会叫它的那些人还活着的时候有效。

changes.after: 所以这个人的处境是：在这个山谷里，能说明他曾经在这里的凭据，很大一部分是一群人嘴上的一个称呼。

changes.before: 而这本书开始的时候，他已经不是那个孩子了。他去了美国，在加利福尼亚待了很多年，做过各种活，后来挣到了钱。书里没有细写那些年——那是这本书处理得很有意思的一处：一个人一生中最"成功"的二十年，被写得极其潦草，几页就过去了。
changes.after: 而这本书开始的时候，他已经不是那个孩子了。他离开山谷约二十年，去过热那亚，也去了美国，在加利福尼亚做过活，后来挣到了钱。书里没有把那二十年一一交代，只写了几个片段。一个人一生中被看作最“成功”的那些年，并不是小说真正要追查的东西。
changes.zh_hant: 而這本書開始的時候，他已經不是那個孩子了。他離開山谷約二十年，去過熱那亞，也去了美國，在加利福尼亞做過活，後來掙到了錢。書裡沒有把那二十年一一交代，只寫了幾個片段。一個人一生中被看作最“成功”的那些年，並不是小說真正要追查的東西。

changes.before: 而他要核对的，是那些年确实发生过，而且他在里面。这一点在书里没有被直说，而它是全书的动力：一个没有出生记录、没有父母、没有姓、只有一个绰号的人，他这一生存在过的全部凭据，是这些坡、这些树、和还记得他的那些人；如果这些东西不在了，那么他的前二十年就没有任何东西可以证明。
changes.after: 而他要核对的，是那些年确实发生过，而且他在里面。这一点在书里没有被直说，却是全书的动力：一个不知道自己从哪里来、在村里只留下一个绰号的人，要找自己早年存在过的证据，能靠的是这些坡、这些树，和还记得他的那些人。如果这些东西不在了，还有什么能替他的前二十年作证？

changes.before: 他叫努托，是鳗鱼小时候的朋友，比他大几岁，是个木匠，会吹单簧管，年轻的时候跟着乐队到处去演出——那是这个山谷里最见过世面的一个人。而努托没有走，他一辈子待在这里：他接了他父亲的木工活，娶了本地的女人，管着这一带的一些事情，什么都知道——谁家出了什么事，哪一年谁死了，战争的时候谁做了什么。
changes.after: 他叫努托，是鳗鱼小时候的朋友，比他大几岁，是个木匠，会吹单簧管，年轻的时候跟着乐队跑过许多地方。在这个山谷里，他是个见过世面的人。而努托没有远走，他在这一带以木工为业，成了家，也一直知道这里发生了什么：谁家出了什么事，哪一年谁死了，战争的时候谁做了什么。

changes.before: The narrator of The Moon and the Bonfires has no given name. People call him Anguilla—Eel—a childhood nickname. Whether he once possessed an official name, the novel never supplies it.
changes.after: The narrator of The Moon and the Bonfires does not give us his name. People call him Anguilla—Eel—a nickname Emilia gave him in his youth. The man can write his name now, he tells us; the reader never sees it.

changes.before: He was abandoned and placed by an orphanage with a poor family at Gaminella. The family received a monthly payment for raising him. When he became old enough to work, the subsidy ended and his value changed form: first income, then labor. The household did not abuse him. He grew beside two girls, worked, and went hungry with them. Each step in the arrangement is defensible. The orphanage found a home it could not provide itself; the family took in a child and needed money.
changes.after: He was abandoned. A poor household at Gaminella took him in, and received a monthly payment for raising him. The money came from the hospital in Alessandria; the household collected five lire at the town hall. By the time he was old enough to work, the money had stopped. What counted now was his labor. He grew up beside two girls, worked, and went hungry with them. Each step in the arrangement is defensible. The hospital found the child a home; a household that needed cash gave him somewhere to grow up.

changes.before: What never enters the arrangement is the question of who the child is. There are no parents, surname, birth story, or record he can later recover. A nickname is useful only while people who know it remain alive. Unlike a family name, it attaches to no archive.
changes.after: What the arrangement does not give him is a way to answer who he is. He does not know his parents or his birthplace. There may still be a file at the town hall. A file is not the same thing as an origin, and a nickname is useful only while somebody knows who it means.

changes.before: Anguilla eventually leaves Italy, spends decades in America, and makes money. The successful years occupy surprisingly little space in the novel. Its real movement begins when he returns to the Piedmont valley and walks from house to farm, tree to road, asking what became of everyone.
changes.after: Anguilla leaves the valley for about twenty years, goes to Genoa and to America, and makes money. Those years appear in fragments. The book’s movement begins when he returns to the Piedmont valley and walks from house to farm, tree to road, asking what became of everyone.

changes.before: He appears to be revisiting home, but he is also searching for evidence. For a person without documentary origins, the slopes and the memories of others are the only witnesses that his first twenty years occurred and that he was inside them.
changes.after: He appears to be revisiting home, but he is also searching for evidence. For someone who does not know where he began, slopes and other people’s memories can testify that his early years happened and that he was in them.

changes.before: Most of the witnesses have vanished. The Gaminella house belongs to another family. The farm at La Mora is empty. People have died, scattered, or fallen silent after fascism, occupation, partisan war, and postwar reprisals. Anguilla can buy land or buildings; locals assume that is why an American returnee has come. Ownership would not answer him. He needs the past fact that he lived here, and no one can sell that fact back.
changes.after: Most of the witnesses have vanished. Another family occupies the Gaminella house; the hazels are gone. La Mora is no longer the household Anguilla knew. People have died, scattered, or fallen silent after fascism, occupation, partisan war, and postwar reprisals. Anguilla can buy property; locals assume that is why a returnee from America has come. Ownership would not answer him. He needs the past fact that he lived here, and no one can sell that fact back.

changes.before: One person remains: Nuto, the carpenter and former clarinet player who never left the valley. He knows who married, who died, which farm changed hands, and what people did during the war. None of this is adequately written down. Nuto himself is the archive.
changes.after: One person remains: Nuto, a carpenter who played the clarinet in a band and kept his life rooted in the valley. He knows who married, who died, which farm changed hands, and what people did during the war. No list of dates could tell these stories. Nuto himself is a living archive.

changes.before: The novel places the traveler and the stayer side by side. Anguilla has money, America, and the freedom to return. Nuto has continuity. Each possesses what the other lacks, but neither can simply transfer it. Anguilla’s journey home becomes a conversation with the last person capable of confirming the life behind his nickname.
changes.after: The novel places the traveler and the stayer side by side. Anguilla has money, America, and the freedom to return. Nuto has continuity. Each possesses what the other lacks, but neither can simply transfer it. Anguilla’s journey home becomes a conversation with someone who can still attest to the life behind his nickname.

changes.before: Nuto embodies that continuity. He took over his father’s carpentry, married locally, and remembers. He is not provincial or naive; he is the novel’s clearest political intelligence. When Anguilla asks what became of a name, Nuto can tell the story because he was present.
changes.after: Nuto embodies that continuity. He works as a carpenter, has a family here, and remembers. He is not provincial or naïve; he has some of the novel’s clearest political judgments. When Anguilla asks what became of a name, Nuto can tell him what he saw or heard.

changes.before: Yet Anguilla cannot simply return to Nuto’s life. Villagers see an American with money and foreign habits. He recognizes every road while the people on those roads do not recognize him. He sees the poverty with an outsider’s eyes. He wants the village and can no longer live inside it as the boy who left.
changes.after: Yet Anguilla cannot simply return to Nuto’s life. The villagers call him the American; some recognize him as the boy from La Mora. He knows the roads, but being recognized is not the same as return. He sees the poverty with an outsider’s eyes. He wants the village and can no longer live inside it as the boy who left.

changes.before: Bonfires introduce rupture into repetition. Fields are burned so ash may enrich the soil; old growth is destroyed for new growth. Rural custom adds rain and renewal to the practical effect. The cycle continues by consuming particular things.
changes.after: Bonfires introduce rupture into repetition. People burn stubble, and Nuto is convinced the fires wake the soil. The novel lets its characters disagree about the custom. In one reading, the cycle continues by consuming particular things.

changes.before: For the valley, this can look like endurance. Crops return, work resumes, other families occupy old houses. For an individual it is merciless. The landscape’s continuity does not preserve the people who once gave it meaning. It ensures that someone will plant again, not that the same person will return.
changes.after: For the valley, this can look like endurance. Crops return, work resumes, other families occupy old houses. For an individual it is merciless. The landscape’s continuity does not preserve all the people who once gave it meaning. Someone will plant again; that is no promise that the same person will return.

changes.before: 伊雷内嫁了，嫁给一个据说条件不错的人——那是家里张罗的，是那门"嫁得好"的亲事；而那个人后来把家产败光了，还打她。书里写努托说这件事的语气是平的：她过得很苦，后来病死了。西尔维娅怀了孕，那是跟一个不能结婚的人；她去打了胎，然后死了。书里没有细写那个过程，努托只说了几句，说她死得很惨，说那件事在当时是不能声张的。
changes.after: 伊雷内嫁给了阿图罗。阿图罗早就追求过她，她不愿意，马泰奥先生起初也反对。后来老人病得不能管事，阿图罗终于占了上风。他卖掉产业，耗光了嫁妆，还打她。鳗鱼回来时，伊雷内也已不在。西尔维娅怀了孕，瞒着家里去找一个接生婆打胎，回来后流血不止，死的时候低声叫着爸爸。
changes.zh_hant: 伊雷內嫁給了阿圖羅。阿圖羅早就追求過她，她不願意，馬泰奧先生起初也反對。後來老人病得不能管事，阿圖羅終於佔了上風。他賣掉產業，耗光了嫁妝，還打她。鰻魚回來時，伊雷內也已不在。西爾維婭懷了孕，瞞著家裡去找一個接生婆打胎，回來後流血不止，死的時候低聲叫著爸爸。

changes.before: 而这两条线加起来，是这本书对那个家最狠的一次判断。这两个女儿走的是两条相反的路，而下场是一样的——伊雷内是听话的那一个：她按规矩来，她被家里安排，她嫁了家里挑的人，而那门亲事把她毁了；西尔维娅是不听话的那一个：她自己来，她不按规矩，她跟她想跟的人在一起，而那件事也把她毁了。在那套安排里，服从和不服从，通向同一个地方。

changes.before: When he returns decades later, Nuto supplies their endings. Irene entered the respectable marriage chosen for her. Her husband ruined the property and beat her; she died ill and miserable. Silvia became pregnant by a man she could not marry, underwent a clandestine abortion, and died.
changes.after: When he returns, the stories of their deaths come out. Irene married Arturo, whom she had not wanted and whom her father had initially opposed. After her father fell ill, Arturo got his way, squandered the dowry, and beat her. She is dead when Anguilla returns. Silvia became pregnant, went secretly to a midwife, and bled to death after returning home.

changes.before: The obedient and disobedient daughters take opposite routes to the same end. Their father was not designing Irene’s destruction. He judged by the available measures of a good match: family, property, respectability. The absent measure was Irene’s own life inside the marriage.
changes.after: The two daughters take different roads. Irene had resisted Arturo, but entered the marriage all the same. Elvira first approved of him, then wanted to keep the dowry at home; Arturo turned the household’s changed fortunes to his advantage. Silvia took matters into her own hands, but could do so only in secret. Neither daughter’s wishes were enough to determine what happened to her.

changes.before: La Mora itself collapses. The estate is sold piece by piece and the house stands empty. The poorest house at Gaminella continues to shelter another family; the seemingly permanent estate does not survive two generations.
changes.after: La Mora’s household collapses. Arturo sells property; the people scatter. When Anguilla returns, even the pine by the gate has been cut down. The poorest house at Gaminella still shelters another family. What seemed the more durable life at La Mora has gone.

changes.before: Santa’s story arrives differently. When Anguilla asks, Nuto postpones. Others offer fragments: she grew beautiful, went to Canelli, knew various men during the war, became well known. No one explains her end.
changes.after: Santa’s story arrives differently. When Anguilla asks, Nuto gives him some pieces but holds back the end. Santa grew beautiful, went to Canelli, and spent time among the Black Brigades. Then she disappeared.

changes.before: The silence belongs to the whole valley, not only to Santa. Fascists, Germans, and partisans passed through. Local people chose sides, crossed between sides, informed, fought, and killed one another. After liberation came reckonings that neighbors preferred not to narrate.
changes.after: The silence belongs to the whole valley, not only to Santa. Fascists, Germans, and partisans passed through. Local people chose sides, crossed between sides, informed, fought, and killed one another. Once the fighting was over, not everyone wanted to tell those stories.

changes.before: Irene was destroyed within the approved social road. Silvia was destroyed after leaving it. Santa entered a political conflict larger than the village and was destroyed there. Pavese does not call this fate. He gives each route concrete conditions: a violent husband selected by respectable criteria, a pregnancy rendered unspeakable, a partisan judgment after divided loyalties.
changes.after: Irene was hurt inside a marriage she had not wanted. Silvia tried to find her own way and died after a clandestine abortion. Santa entered a conflict larger than the village and was killed there. Pavese does not call this fate. In each life he shows particular people and pressures: a marriage negotiated through reputation and property, a pregnancy that could not be spoken of, a wartime judgment.

changes.before: Anguilla had once imagined the sisters fortunate because their identities were anchored in family and land. He, the nameless hired boy, survived by leaving; all three recognized daughters died. The reversal proves no comforting law. Poverty does not protect, travel does not guarantee survival, and rootedness is not security.

changes.before: 那是战争最后那一段的事。她那时候二十几岁，长得极好看，人在加内利；而她卷进了那几年的事情里——她跟法西斯那边的人来往，也跟山上的人来往，她替一边送过消息，也替另一边送过。书里没有把她写成一个坏人，也没有写成一个英雄：它写的是一个二十几岁的女人，在一个所有人都在选边的年份里，两边都沾了。
changes.after: 那是战争最后那一段的事。桑塔在加内利，在法西斯那边做事，也给抵抗者送过消息，后来真的上山参加游击队。努托讲她曾经跟指挥官巴拉卡一起脱险；后来也是巴拉卡，认定她给对手送了消息，造成过具体的损失。书里没有用一个“坏人”或“英雄”替她收尾，而是让努托把这些放在一起讲。

changes.before: Cinto lives in the same ruined house where Anguilla grew up, on the same slope beneath the same tree. His family are tenant farmers. He has a disabled leg and cannot even become the pair of working hands into which Anguilla’s foster subsidy once converted him.
changes.after: Cinto lives in the same house where Anguilla grew up, on the same slope. The old hazels are gone. His father Valino is a widower. Cinto lives with him, with Valino’s sister-in-law Rosina, and with an older woman he calls his grandmother. They work land whose crops must be divided with the owner. Cinto has a disabled leg and cannot easily do the labor for which Anguilla’s foster household once counted on him.

changes.before: Anguilla visits, brings gifts, and describes American trains, cities, and work. He wants Cinto to know that other places exist and that departure is imaginable. Yet the child’s path is narrower than his had been.
changes.after: Anguilla visits and describes the port at Genoa, the ships and the work on them. He wants Cinto to know that other places exist and that leaving is imaginable. Yet the child’s path is narrower than his had been.

changes.before: One night Cinto’s father Valino kills the women in the household, sets fire to the house, and hangs himself. Cinto runs down the dark hill with a knife in his hand.
changes.after: One evening, after a quarrel over the division of beans and potatoes, Valino attacks Rosina and sets fire to the house. Rosina and the older woman die. Cinto escapes his father and hides outside, knife in hand. Later he sees his father hanging from a walnut tree.

changes.before: Valino has spent a life working poor soil under fixed rent, growing older without any institution designed to receive failure, illness, or exhaustion. This does not excuse the murders. It prevents the event from being flattened into the sudden revelation of an inexplicable monster. No landlord needs to break a law for a family to be carried year after year to a point where nothing in the arrangement can catch them.
changes.after: The novel puts years of want, the reckoning over the crop, and the man’s violence close together. It does not excuse him. Nor does it make the violence a revelation that comes out of nowhere. Even after the fire the owner wants the surviving child to make good the loss. The arrangement can still account for the property; it has no place ready for the boy.

changes.before: Afterward Nuto finally tells what happened to Santa. During the war she moved among fascists and partisans, carried information, and touched both sides. The partisans judged her a collaborator, shot her, and burned the body.
changes.after: Afterward Nuto finally tells what happened to Santa. She moved between the Fascists and the resistance, passing information, and at one point joined the partisans in the hills. Baracca told Nuto that she had been informing for the other side and named the losses he held her responsible for. He read the sentence. Santa tried to flee; Nuto heard the shots. The men then burned her body.

changes.before: They wanted no grave. A grave would provide a place to visit, remember, and contest what she had been. Burning the body was meant to remove not only a person but the site from which another account might begin.
changes.after: Nuto was there and helped. He tells Anguilla that they will not find her. For a reader, the lack of a grave also means the absence of a place to visit, remember, and tell the story differently.

changes.before: The novel’s fires now separate into three meanings. Field bonfires destroy so growth can return. Valino’s fire ends a trapped household. Santa’s pyre aims to make someone leave no trace at all.
changes.after: The novel’s fires can now be read three ways. The fires on the fields are meant to make growth return. Valino’s fire ends a trapped household. Santa’s pyre leaves no grave to find, only a mark on the ground.

changes.before: This is the completion of Anguilla’s fear. He has no parents, surname, or birth record and depends on remembered testimony. Santa had a father, a family name, and a recognized childhood, yet can still be reduced to one reluctant witness’s memory. If Nuto dies without speaking, the human being behind the political judgment disappears.
changes.after: This is a sharper form of Anguilla’s fear. He does not know his parents or his birthplace, and needs other people’s testimony to tell the story of his life here. Santa had a father and a recognized childhood, yet there is no grave to look for. Without Nuto’s account, Anguilla would not know what happened on that hillside.

changes.before: Pavese supplies no large exit. Anguilla neither settles nor announces another departure. He does not adopt Cinto. He and Nuto discuss finding the boy an apprenticeship, perhaps in carpentry. It is the novel’s smallest forward act: a place where one disabled child might learn work that does not require the body the hillside demanded.
changes.after: Pavese supplies no large exit. Earlier, Nuto actually takes Cinto into his home to learn carpentry and music. Anguilla plans to go back to Genoa and says there may one day be a place for the boy there. They consider taking him to have his leg examined. It is a small thing that has already begun. It does not undo what the last passage brings back: Nuto’s memory of the ash and the mark of the fire.

changes.before: Pavese published this final novel in April 1950 and died by suicide that August. Biography is often used to seal the book in despair. But the order matters. He first completed the work: placed the three fires together, preserved Santa in words, and ended with two men considering one child’s next step. The writer’s later death does not cancel the action the finished novel continues to perform in his absence.
changes.after: Pavese published this final novel in April 1950 and died by suicide that August. Biography is often used to seal the book in despair. But the order matters. He first completed the work: set the three fires beside one another, preserved Santa in words, put one child in a place where he might learn a trade, and ended on the trace of a fire. The writer’s later death does not cancel the action the finished novel continues to perform in his absence.
